items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Even if it’s Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman, and all those people, Count Basie and Duke Ellington, listen to those regularly as kids are starting to listen to that

ctx.x: Do you see a good future for this music in general, for jazz? I see so much publicity about it but I don’t see it transferred to live venues.

Well I see a future, I really do. Because I think there’s going to be I should say evolution but a revolution. You see part of it now would be kids starting the swing dancing things, suddenly you’re pushing bands back. Even if it’s Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman, and all those people, Count Basie and Duke Ellington, listen to those regularly as kids are starting to listen to that, in that swing dance situation. So then you’ll have groups, college groups, having swing bands. And it will evolve, it will go all the way…
So people can get involved, as you said.
